plan.summary: This 1-4 block starts the 12-week off-camp build for boxing with one focused full-body S&C session each week. Week 1 establishes training maxes for the main lower-body lift so later percentage work is anchored to a real baseline, and the main training starts in Week 2. With only one gym day and a preference for more conditioning, the session keeps power and strength first, then uses brief accessories and simple conditioning that support boxing without creating unnecessary fatigue.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build basic full-body strength and general power while keeping conditioning supportive and recoverable.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress the main lifts and power work with slightly higher intensity while controlling fatigue around boxing practice.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Keep strength in place and express it through faster, sharper power and conditioning work for boxing.

exercises.name: 1a. Box Jump
exercises.notes: Use a box height you can land on quietly and confidently. Reset between reps and keep each jump fast and crisp.

substitutionOptions.name: Countermovement Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if box setup is awkward. Land softly and reset each rep.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if you want a simpler low-impact option.

exercises.name: 1b. Medicine Ball Rotational Scoop Throw
exercises.notes: Throw hard from the hips, not just the arms. Use a non-bouncing or low-bouncing ball and reset between reps.

substitutionOptions.name: Medicine Ball Shot-Put Throw
substitutionOptions.notes: Good substitute if wall space is limited.

substitutionOptions.name: Half-Kneeling Rotational Throw
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if you need a simpler setup with less lower-body involvement.

exercises.name: 2. Back Squat
exercises.notes: Brace hard, squat to a consistent depth, and stop if technique breaks. This session establishes your baseline for future percentage work.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively, then work up to your heaviest clean set of 3-5 reps. Log the load and reps so the app can estimate your training max.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track the heaviest clean top set with solid depth and control.

substitutionOptions.name: Safety Bar Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if shoulder mobility or bar position is uncomfortable.

substitutionOptions.name: Goblet Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use only if barbell squatting is not yet comfortable. Keep it heavy but technically clean.

exercises.name: 3a. Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.notes: Control the lowering, pause briefly at the bottom, and drive up hard. Leave 2 reps in reserve.

substitutionOptions.name: Barbell Bench Press
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if you are comfortable with barbell bench technique.

substitutionOptions.name: Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if you want a simpler option with less setup.

exercises.name: 3b. Chest-Supported Row
exercises.notes: Pull the elbow back without shrugging. Squeeze at the top and keep the torso still.

substitutionOptions.name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Good substitute if the bench station is busy.

substitutionOptions.name: Seated Cable Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if you want a stable, easy-to-learn option.

exercises.name: 4. Romanian Deadlift
exercises.notes: Push the hips back, keep a soft knee bend, and stop when you lose a flat back. Leave 2 reps in reserve.

substitutionOptions.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
substitutionOptions.notes: Simpler to learn and easier to control.

substitutionOptions.name: 45-Degree Back Extension
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if hinging with a bar is still inconsistent.

exercises.name: 5. Ab Wheel Rollout
exercises.notes: Keep ribs down and glutes tight. Only roll out as far as you can without losing trunk position.

substitutionOptions.name: Stability Ball Rollout
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if the ab wheel is too difficult.

substitutionOptions.name: Cable Crunch
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if shoulder comfort limits rollouts.

exercises.name: 6. Assault Bike Intervals
exercises.notes: Work hard but stay smooth. Keep output even across rounds and finish feeling worked, not wrecked.

endurancePrescription.structure: 8 rounds of 15 seconds hard, 45 seconds easy
endurancePrescription.intensity: Hard on work bouts, easy spin on recovery
